label: D1 after a2->S1 rewarded (rare), growing over episode, collapses at end
explanation: Fires only at D1 and essentially only when the previous trial was a2 -> S1 (rare) rewarded; residual after that pattern is +0.51 versus about -0.04 after every other pattern, including the other rare-rewarded case a1 S2 r. Magnitude after a2 S1 r grows with episode time (near 0 in trials 0-9, peaking at about 1 in trials 60-79, down to about 0.6 in 80-89 and near 0 in 90-99). That interaction (fitted weight +0.97) carries almost all of the fit. A rewarded trial before that adds a little (+0.05). After other patterns it is near zero, so the per-decile timing baseline is removed for them (-0.05). GO and D2 are always 0. Policy, value, hidden good state and future variables add essentially nothing. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.71, above the additive all ceiling of 0.48 because the pattern x episode-time interaction is not additive. Misses left over: D1 firing on the first window trial where the previous trial is outside the window.

issues: The core claim holds. The original 3 terms reproduce test R^2 beyond timing 0.707 (weights +0.96, +0.045, -0.048). The D1-only claim and the episode-time shape after a2 S1 r both check out.

It overclaims that the feature is 'almost only' a2->S1 rewarded (rare). The worst dev misses include D1 activations of 0.91 (t75), 0.89 (t57), 0.78 (t49) and 0.58 (t72) after a COMMON a1 S1 r trial that followed a2 trials. Adding the term (D1) * last_is('a1 S1 r') * (tv('action',-2)==2) * ep_dec-shape gets weight +0.48 (about half the a2 S1 r peak) and raises test R^2 from 0.707 to 0.734. The same pattern preceded by an a1 trial gets weight about 0.01, so it adds nothing.

a2 S1 r is not uniform. When the trial two back was a1 (the agent had just switched to a2), the response is much weaker. The split term gets weight -0.42 on top of the base, or about 0.63 against 1.05 when it is fitted separately, and test R^2 rises to 0.746. Using tv('stay',-1)==0 instead gives the same result.

Taken together, the variable behind the magnitude is better described as 'S1 just paid a reward while the agent had been choosing a2', i.e. evidence against an S2 belief. The rare transition label is too narrow. a1 S2 r, the other rare-rewarded pattern, really is near zero, so the effect is specific to S1 and is not about rare transitions in general.

The rewarded-two-back term (+0.04 to +0.05) is minor but holds. A term for the window's first trial (trial==0 with in_rew==1, times ep_dec) adds nothing (weight 0.002), so the stated leftover from first-trial D1 steps cannot be captured with observed cues. In misses it is a small over-prediction (-0.011).
After the fix, misses show only small systematic errors (largest D1 after a2 S1 r -0.023, D1 after a1 S1 r +0.010). No large error class remains.
